title: Bhishma's fall
hook: the Kaurava commander loves the men he is fighting, and Duryodhana's friend Karna refuses to fight under him.
carry: a man who dies only when he chooses

segments.voice: Yesterday Yudhishthira walked unarmed to Bhishma for his blessing, and the grandsire told him: ask me again another time.

An army might want a commander who hates the enemy. Duryodhana's commander doesn't. When Duryodhana asked Bhishma to lead his forces, in the Udyoga book, the old man said yes, and then set terms. The sons of Pandu, he said, are as dear to me as you are. I will fight their armies for you. I will not kill them. And there was a second problem, standing right there in the hall: Karna. Today, Bhishma's fall begins, with the strange shape of the side he leads.
screen: `A COMMANDER WHO DOESN'T HATE` → `HIS TERMS: NOT THE FIVE BROTHERS` → `AND KARNA IN THE HALL`

segments.voice: Start with Karna. Bhishma and Karna don't get along. In the Udyoga book, when Bhishma ranks the warriors on his own side, he rates Karna low, and Karna is stung. So when Bhishma takes command, Karna makes a vow of his own. As long as Bhishma lives, Karna will not fight. When Bhishma falls, then he'll take the field against Arjuna. So the Kaurava side goes into battle with its commander holding back from the five brothers, and Karna sitting in his tent. Now add something the epic told us long ago. When Bhishma was young, he gave up his claim to the throne and swore never to marry, so his father could marry again. In return, the epic says, his father gave him a gift: death would not take him until he chose it. Put those together and you have the riddle of the next days. Bhishma can't be beaten, and he won't be hurried. In the first day's fighting, the losses fall hard on the Pandava side. Uttara, the young prince of Virata, who held the reins for Arjuna in the cattle raid, is killed. So is his brother Shveta, at Bhishma's own hand. The family that sheltered the Pandavas pays first. So hold Bhishma's fall as a question, not just an event. How do you bring down a man who loves you, who can't be beaten, and who decides for himself when he dies? The epic takes its time answering.
screen: `KARNA WON'T FIGHT WHILE BHISHMA LIVES` · `THE BOON: DEATH WHEN HE CHOOSES` · `VIRATA'S SONS FALL FIRST` · then, large: `HOW DO YOU BRING HIM DOWN?`

segments.voice: Think of a commitment you carry, a job, a promise, a family role, that sometimes pulls against what you'd rather do. Breathing in, feel its weight honestly; breathing out, notice what in you still chooses to keep it, and let both be true, the way Bhishma held two loyalties on the same field. If you pray, you can bring that commitment with you.
Bhishma's fall. Not yet. Today it's a riddle: a commander who loves the other side, and who will die only when he chooses.
Your line: a man who dies only when he chooses. The riddle is set, and the answer will take days. Day eight hundred twenty-five, done.

howItsDone: Bhishma's terms as commander, Karna's refusal to fight under him, and the boon that lets him choose his death are told in the Mahabharata's Udyoga, Adi and Bhishma books, and are familiar parts of retellings of the war.

chat.says: Why was Bhishma such a strange commander for Duryodhana's side?
options: He loved the Pandavas: he'd fight their armies, but not kill the five brothers.
He secretly fought for the Pandavas and passed them his battle plans.
He was too old to fight, so he gave orders from his tent instead.
chat.meaning: Bhishma took command on terms: the sons of Pandu were dear to him, and he would not kill them. Karna, stung, would not fight while he lived.

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Bhishma's terms on accepting command (the sons of Pandu dear to him; he will not slay them); Bhishma rating Karna an ardharatha (half-car warrior) and Karna's vow not to fight while Bhishma lives.
Confirm: Shantanu's boon that death would not come to Bhishma until he wished it (Adi Parva).
